analysis.investment_thesis: Aurionpro is a fast-emerging fintech infrastructure play riding India's banking digitization wave — revenue has compounded ~32% annually since FY2022, and the forward PEG of ~0.6 (Forward P/E 16.94 vs ~28% recent earnings CAGR) is genuinely attractive for Lynch-style GARP. However, a decade of stagnation (FY2016–FY2021 revenue barely moved), erratic historical profitability, and aggressive M&A-funded expansion (₹421 Cr investing outflow in FY2025) demand proof that this acceleration is structural before deploying serious capital.
key_strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.02, borrowings collapsed from ₹154 Cr to ₹30 Cr) gives room for growth without financial strain.
Compelling PEG: Forward P/E ~17 against ~28-35% recent earnings CAGR puts the PEG well below 0.8 — Lynch's sweet spot.
Clear niche story: banking/trade-finance SaaS (iCashpro, Fintra, integro) in a massive India + APAC digital banking TAM with embedded switching costs.
key_risks: Thin gross margins (27.88%) expose a significant hardware/equipment revenue mix — this isn't a pure-software story, which caps margin expansion.
Promoter skin-in-the-game is low at 26.88%; management doesn't have a strong ownership-aligned incentive to protect minority shareholders.
Aggressive acquisitions (₹421 Cr investing CF in FY2025, equity raises funding it) risk integration failures and EPS dilution — classic destroyer of fast-grower stories.
red_flags: FY2021 net loss of ₹192 Cr and erratic 'Other Income' swings (₹82 Cr gain in FY2018, -₹118 Cr in FY2021) suggest one-time adjustments that obscure true earnings quality.
9-year revenue CAGR is only 5.7% — the acceleration is a 3-year phenomenon, not a proven multi-cycle track record.
FCF compressed sharply in FY2025 (₹62 Cr vs ₹131 Cr in FY2024) as capex surged to ₹95 Cr — watch whether this is investment for growth or cost creep.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
As Peter Lynch, I'd classify Aurionpro as an emerging fast grower — but one I'd want to watch from the dugout before fully committing. The recent numbers are genuinely exciting: revenue went from ₹374 Cr (FY2021) to ₹1,173 Cr (FY2025), a ~33% CAGR; net profit compounded ~35% over the same stretch; and the company is essentially debt-free with ₹269 Cr of cash. The story is simple enough — banks across India and APAC need digital plumbing (transaction banking, trade finance, lending origination, AI decisioning), and Aurionpro sells exactly that. At a forward P/E of ~17 with ~28-30% earnings growth implied, the PEG hovers around 0.6, which is the kind of number that makes my ears perk up.

What holds me back from a strong buy is the institutional memory of FY2016–FY2021, where revenue went nowhere and the company posted a massive ₹192 Cr loss in FY2021. The business has been restructured and refocused, but Lynch's rule applies: a company that stumbled for half a decade needs to prove the new chapter is real, not just a rerating. The gross margin of 27.88% also tells me this isn't a clean software compounder — equipment and project revenue dilute the economics. And the ₹421 Cr of investing outflows in FY2025, funded by equity raises (₹283 Cr financing inflow), smells like acquisition-driven growth that could reverse if integrations disappoint. I'd own a small position and watch the next two quarters for margin expansion and organic order flow proof.
